root_motivation: Joe 2026-10-01, 'we have to make this much simpler': the bare `claude mcp add --transport http mcphost https://mcphost.dev/mcp` snippet leaves the agent on a connection where every host.* call fails tenant_key_missing until a human relays signup/tenant_key by hand. Three of the four homepage snippets produce exactly this dead connection, and the 30.7s signup-to-publish median never starts for an agent nobody coached. Every other hosted MCP hands the client a working endpoint on first contact, so an uncoached first failure reads as broken, not unauthenticated. Session binding after signup already exists (PRD-mcphost-session-bound-tenant-after-signup); the only missing piece is making that binding happen without the agent asking, reusing signup's own limiter/kill-switch/fleet-IP classification as the abuse control.
user_persona: An agent operator who configures the bare endpoint with one claude mcp add line and expects it to just work; a person who never wants to learn what tenant_key means; the operator who needs implicit tenants to carry source: implicit and obey the same per-IP limiter and pause file as explicit signup, so a crawler cannot mint unlimited tenants.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a fresh streamable-HTTP session on /mcp with no header, When host.tool_publish is called with a valid echo spec, Then the tool is published under a new tenant, the result carries onboarding.url and onboarding.tenant, and host.whoami on the same session returns that tenant with source: "implicit".
Given the same session, When a second host.* call runs, Then its result carries no onboarding field.

Given one IP that has created the limiter's maximum tenants this hour, When an anonymous host.* call arrives, Then the error class is signup_rate_limited, data.help ends in /u/new, data.retry_after_s is present, and no tenant or tool was created.
Given the signup pause file is present, When an anonymous host.* call arrives, Then signup_paused is returned within 1s and nothing is created.
Given an anonymous session, When tools/list, initialize, signup, host.redeem, host.quickstart, or billing.plans are called, Then no tenant is created.
Given a request with an unknown tenant_key, When dispatched, Then tenant_key_invalid is returned and no tenant is created.

Given the synthorg journey and tool-surface conformance harnesses at the landing commit, When run against a build of this PRD, Then no assertion expects tenant_key_missing on /mcp and both runs are green on the fixture host (both harnesses live in ~/repos/synthorg and run hermetically against their own in-process fixture host; this repo pins the behavioral contract they assert).

five_whys_trace.q: Why call the existing control::signup() rather than writing new tenant-creation logic for the implicit path?
five_whys_trace.a: Technical Considerations is explicit: the per-IP limiter is the single choke point and this PRD adds no second limiter -- signup() already owns the rate limit, pause-file kill switch, and fleet-IP/synthetic classification a new code path would have to reimplement and could drift from.

five_whys_trace.q: Why guard the new match arm with tenant_path_namespace(parts).is_none() instead of letting it fire on any host.*/billing.* call?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 4 names bare /mcp specifically ('no longer reachable for host.*/billing.* on /mcp'); PRD-mcphost-tenant-resource-metadata's per-tenant 401 challenge on /t/{ns}/mcp is a separate, still-valid contract this PRD must not silently break.

five_whys_trace.q: Why dispatch the triggering call AFTER binding, in the same request, instead of returning a 'you've been signed up, try again' response?
five_whys_trace.a: Technical Considerations: 'the call that triggered creation must be executed after binding in the same request so the agent sees its real result plus onboarding, not a separate signed up response' -- a second round trip is exactly the friction this PRD exists to remove.

five_whys_trace.q: Why update ~19 pre-existing tests that pinned the old tenant_key_missing-on-bare-/mcp contract, rather than leaving them red for their own PRDs' owners to fix?
five_whys_trace.a: This dispatch's own gate (a) is 'full cargo test is green' with no carve-out, and the PRD's Migration/compatibility section explicitly sanctions exactly this update ('Clients that depended on tenant_key_missing as a probe ... must be updated'); the prior abandoned direct-build left these red and called it 'the single biggest blocker to landing' -- repeating that choice would just defer the same blocker again.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a bare call that implicitly signs up upgrade its HTTP response to text/event-stream, and why does that matter for the test fixes?
five_whys_trace.a: Binding the session emits notifications/tools/list_changed before the real result, which rmcp's own transport upgrades from application/json to text/event-stream (the same thing signup/host.redeem already trigger) -- three tests that read a raw reqwest::Response directly needed a content-type-aware parse instead of assuming plain JSON, once their bare call started binding a session for the first time.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Default implicit tenant name: agent-<ulid> or derived from the MCP client's initialize.clientInfo.name?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: clientInfo.name when present, else agent-<8-char ulid suffix>, per the PRD's own open-question draft resolution.

ambiguities_resolved.question: AC7 names the synthorg journey harness and the tool-surface conformance harness -- outside this repo/worktree, but are they actually unreachable from this sandbox?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- both are real, identifiable modules in ~/repos/synthorg (journey_client.py / toolconf.py), reachable on the local filesystem and runnable hermetically (an in-process fixture transport, no live mcphost deploy needed). Pinned the exact behavioral contract those harnesses depend on with a local regression sweep (implsign_ac07) in THIS repo, fixed every pre-existing in-repo test the PRD's own Migration note flags, AND fixed toolconf.py's own no_key probe (it still scored the old tenant_key_missing refusal a pass and the new implicit-signup success a leak) plus every synthorg-side test that pinned that obsolete contract -- committed there (7b610cb, master, not pushed). See docs/receipts/implsign-ac07-synthorg-cross-repo.md and agent/test-map.json's AC7 entry.

ambiguities_resolved.question: requirement 5 says host.quickstart's description should stop claiming tenant_key_missing, but host.quickstart's description text ('Unauthenticated callers get the signup step first.') was already accurate and unrelated to the claim -- what actually needed rewriting?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: host.quickstart itself is on the Non-goals exempt list (never implicit-signs-up) and its description was never inaccurate; the actual stale tenant_key_missing claims were host_schema's tenant_key property description, get_info's instructions, and host.quickstart's own unauthenticated-branch note text (control::quickstart) -- all three rewritten, the tool's top-level description left untouched.
